threads.body: If the GraphQL response includes an `errors` field or `data.repository` is null (e.g., bad `repo`, auth/rate-limit issues, or partial failures), this function will currently treat it as “no matching issue” and return `None`, which then triggers creation of a duplicate dashboard issue. Consider explicitly checking for `errors`/missing repository and raising an exception so the workflow fails loudly instead of creating a new issue on query failure.

replies.body: Looked into this. `gh api graphql` already exits non-zero whenever the response includes an `errors` array — verified: querying a nonexistent repo returns `{"data":{"repository":null},"errors":[{"type":"NOT_FOUND",...}]}` with exit code 1, which `gh_graphql` / `run_gh` turn into a `RuntimeError`. The original silent-fallback path was the actual bug, because `or {}` papered over a null repository and converted "loud failure" into "duplicate dashboard issue". Fixed in b6f25b1 by removing the silent fallbacks entirely (`or {}`, `or []`, `isinstance` defenses) — now subscript access fails fast at the assumption boundary, and `gh_graphql` remains the fail-fast layer for any GraphQL error.

threads.body: The pagination loop can become infinite if `pageInfo.hasNextPage` is true but `pageInfo.endCursor` is missing/empty (since `after` becomes `None` and the next iteration re-fetches the first page). Add a guard to raise/abort when `hasNextPage` is true but `endCursor` is not a non-empty string.

replies.body: Not taking this one. Per the [Relay Cursor Connections spec](https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm) (which GitHub implements), `endCursor` is the cursor of the last edge in the current page — it is `null` only when the page has zero edges, and in that case `hasNextPage` is also `false`. The hypothesized state (`hasNextPage: true` AND `endCursor: null/empty`) is unreachable on a spec-compliant connection, so guarding for it would be defensive code for a scenario that cannot happen. If GitHub ever did violate this, `gh_graphql` would still raise on the next page request (an empty `after=` is rejected), preserving fail-fast behavior.

threads.body: `find_dashboard_issue()` paginates through *all* open issues with the `dashboard` label, even though the query is already ordered by `CREATED_AT ASC` and you only need the earliest issue whose title matches `DASHBOARD_TITLE`. Consider returning immediately when you encounter the first matching node (and dropping the `numbers` list / `min()`), to reduce GraphQL calls and avoid scanning the full result set unnecessarily.
